As Director of Investor Relations at Together, you will own the company's relationships with its investors and shape how the equity capital markets understand Together's business, strategy, and long-term opportunity. Reporting to the VP of FP&A, and partnering closely with the CEO, CFO, and executive team, you will be responsible for building our investor engagement strategy and investment narrative.

You will also own the core planning and reporting work that underpins our investor story: board reporting, the long-range plan, and the KPIs we use to run and describe the business. This hybrid investor relations and FP&A role will provide deep and unique insight into building and scaling an AI inference company.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role in a lean function: you will build investor relations at Together largely from the ground up. This role is well suited to someone with analytical rigor and a background in equity capital markets who follows developments in technology and AI closely. You will be responsible for deeply understanding investors' perspectives on Together as well as the broader industry, bringing strategic insights to leadership to help inform key decisions. Strong candidates pair depth in financial analysis with the ability to distill sophisticated financial and technical concepts into clear and concise investor narratives.

About the Role

Together AI is building the AI-native cloud — the fastest inference infrastructure on the planet, paired with a model ecosystem, orchestration layer, and data center footprint that enterprises and frontier labs depend on. As we expand the surface area through which our models and inference reach end users, we're hiring a Head of Distribution Partnerships to source and build the 0-to-1 partnerships that drive token distribution from models served on Together.

This is a builder role for someone with sharp technical instincts and a strong product-partnerships background who can identify where Together's competitive edge in open-source model serving complements another platform's distribution — and then go build that relationship from scratch. You'll work across technology partnerships, co-sell motions, ISV integrations, and OEM arrangements with data platforms, cloud providers, and software ecosystems where our inference and OSS model serving capabilities create obvious joint value.

You need technical fluency to scope integrations with engineering counterparts, product instincts to identify where Together's serving stack creates a compelling wedge, and the hustle to turn a cold outreach into a signed, launched partnership. You'll report into the VP of Strategic Partnerships and work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and the broader Partnerships team.

Responsibilities 

• Source and Build 0-to-1 Partnerships: Identify and prioritize distribution partners — data platforms, cloud marketplaces, ISVs, and software ecosystems — where Together's open-source model serving and inference performance is a differentiated fit. Build these relationships from first contact through signed agreement and launch.

About the Role

Together AI is looking for a Manager to own the commercial relationships with our international cloud compute suppliers and the market intelligence that drives our compute supply strategy. You will manage the lifecycle of international cloud service provider (CSP) contracts and renewals, run RFP processes for new capacity, build pricing benchmarks across the global GPU cloud landscape, and partner with infrastructure engineering, finance, and GTM to secure the right capacity at the best economics as we rapidly scale our GPU fleet globally. 

Responsibilities

• Manage the lifecycle of international CSP leasing agreements, from sourcing and RFPs through contract execution and renewals

• Partner with infrastructure engineering to translate technical requirements into commercial specifications, and coordinate technical evaluations during vendor selection

• Develop and maintain relationships with cloud compute suppliers to expand Together's vendor ecosystem into new international markets

• Build and maintain market intelligence to stay ahead of pricing trends, supply availability, and the evolving international cloud compute vendor landscape

• Develop negotiation strategies that improve our cost position and terms as we scale, accounting for local contracting norms and market dynamics

• Drive continuous improvement on Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) and actively mitigate supply chain and commercial risks across the GPU fleet

• Establish and lead regular, structured vendor performance reviews, including Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), with international cloud and infrastructure compute suppliers.

• Track the country-level factors that shape international capacity decisions, including power availability, local regulatory and data residency requirements
